dimension.eligibility: Captured biome-source overlap with the resolved retained End biome tag, plus the custom generator height condition. EndJigsawStructure.findGenerationPoint samples start_height, then, because project_start_to_heightmap is absent, queries WORLD_SURFACE_WG at chunk minimum X/Z and adds the sampled offset. This is a surface-relative start, not absolute Y=0 or observed exposure.

It scans upward from minAbsoluteHeight+sampledOffset through maxAbsoluteHeight, selecting the first Y with non-air at Y-1 and air at Y and Y+2 (Y+1 is not explicitly tested). grouping_decision.name: AdoraBuild furnished Overworld houses
grouping_decision.rationale: Thirty-two standalone furnished Overworld house variants retain a common enclosed building role across wood and sandstone materials. Complete comparisons preserve gabled cottages, flat or stepped roofs, porches, multi-level rooms and planted roofs as layout variants, rather than multiplying families for roof shape or furnishing alone. All thirty-two roots use surface projection with zero start offset, beard-box adaptation and empty spawn overrides. Most include beds and domestic workstations; oak_house_large_1 and oak_house_medium_1 instead retain book/lectern or barrel/pot furnishings without a bed, so this grouping does not assert sleeping facilities in every variant. Village loot, food caches, bee content and authored domestic animals remain variant-specific. Distinct raised-room access, the low terrain-enclosed hut, bamboo cache and End/Nether designs are separated. Canonical design and required source descriptions are assessed. Placement success, realized populations, mechanism operation and visibility distances are not claimed.

grouping_decision.name: AdoraBuild nether fortress
grouping_decision.rationale: One modular nether-brick tower, stair and bridge network. Its eight reachable templates are assembly components, including alternative tower heights and chest-bearing pieces, not separate families. The standalone courtyard and roofed wart building are separated because they have distinct complete layouts rather than being parts of this network. The full piece-bounded fortress monster override and fixed start height remain preserved. Canonical design and required source descriptions are assessed. Saved-layout chunk stages and the basalt connector defect remain explicit; generated populations and visibility are not claimed.

dimension.eligibility: Resolved biome-source overlap and custom column-search constraints identify eligible placement. NetherJigsawStructure.findGenerationPoint queries the base column at chunk minimum X/Z. It scans upward from minAbsoluteHeight+sampledOffset through maxAbsoluteHeight, selecting the first Y with non-air at Y-1 and air at Y and Y+2 (Y+1 is not explicitly tested). It rejects no match, then starts at selectedY+offset and delegates JigsawPlacement.addPieces. All these roots use offset 0, min 32, max 96, no projection and beard_box adaptation. Non-air support can include fluid; this is not a guaranteed solid floor or measured clearance.

dimension.eligibility: Resolved biome-source overlap and custom column-search constraints identify eligible placement. NetherJigsawStructure.findGenerationPoint queries the base column at chunk minimum X/Z. It scans upward from minAbsoluteHeight+sampledOffset through maxAbsoluteHeight, selecting the first Y with non-air at Y-1 and air at Y and Y+2 (Y+1 is not explicitly tested). It rejects no match, then starts at selectedY+offset and delegates JigsawPlacement.addPieces. All these roots use offset 0, min 32, max 96, no projection and beard_box adaptation. Non-air support can include fluid; this is not a guaranteed solid floor or measured clearance.

grouping_decision.name: BetterEnd Lake Formation
grouping_decision.rationale: Five registered lake variants form one natural formation family. Normal and rare EndLake classes inherit the base generation implementation and only forward construction and override type(). Megalake and small megalake use LakePiece with different size parameters and terrain checks; EndLake uses EndLakePiece. Preserve both procedural algorithms, all type IDs and biome constraints as variants of the lake formation rather than counting type aliases or size variants as independent families. Their shared lakes generation step and empty spawn overrides do not establish material composition, absence of mobs/loot, actual geometry or encounter frequency. Piece-content interpretation and remaining effective attributes are still required.

grouping_decision.name: IDAS castle
grouping_decision.rationale: One castle-settlement family with three equal-weight authored designs in the same start pool, not three interchangeable material skins. Castle1 is a compact battlemented enclosure, castle2 has a denser tower and courtyard arrangement, and castle3 has a large roofed keep and outer walls. Main template extents are respectively 36 by 23 by 26, 41 by 36 by 53 and 106 by 66 by 84. Their corresponding bottom templates are 36 by 6 by 26, 41 by 1 by 53 and 106 by 3 by 84; each main connects to its own bottom through matching idas:bottom names. All designs connect to the same villager and guard entity-component pools. Castle1 and castle2 additionally connect to plains village town centers; castle3 has no such connector. Preserve all three settlement layouts as design alternatives, consistent with the multi-design village grouping, rather than counting foundations, entity templates or the 136 reachable templates (including shared village pieces) as additional castle families. All three main/bottom pairs lack physical spawners, while their loot and authored contents differ: castle1 includes villagers and farm animals with castle, library and vanilla village loot; castle2 includes guards, mounts, displays, seat and glue with castle, library and throne loot; castle3 includes mounts and displays with castle, bedroom, food, library, throne and borrowed witches-treestump loot. Castle2 retains one authored entity lacking an ID. Shared loot does not merge castle with witches treestump. Keep the common castle processor and distinct element terrain kernels, and preserve the selected village-tavern component link. Component extents and reachability do not prove generated assembly bounds or operating Create machinery. Canonical design relationships are resolved. Effective attributes remain open.

grouping_decision.rationale: One four-component expedition assembly with matching connector chain entrance to tunnel to ruins1 to ruins2. Dining halls, libraries, prisons, portal rooms and other connected pools are components of this structure, not independent families. The Integrated Stronghold and Better Strongholds suppression hooks target vanilla StructureType.STRONGHOLD. This root uses integrated_api:generic_structure and the Better Strongholds root uses yungsapi:yung_jigsaw, so neither matches those vanilla-type filters. Their distinct assembled designs remain separate families, while vanilla is retained as a suppressed candidate. This resolves the replacement boundary without claiming observed placement, completed attributes or an effective Eye of Ender target.

grouping_decision.name: Vanilla village
grouping_decision.rationale: Five biome/material variants share the jigsaw village assembly contract. Houses, roads, mobs and injected buildings require component attribution, not one family per template or profession. Packaged definition identity is preserved; retained-mod hooks, effective content and remaining attributes require reconciliation. Better Village contributes vanilla-ID template replacements to this family: 246 packaged templates, of which 244 are reachable in the selected trace. Snowy streets crossroad_01 and straight_05 remain packaged but untraced. Its four compatibility metadata entries are disabled and target absent mods; they introduce no extra pool content in this stack. The enabled placement hook uses spacing 45, separation 20, salt 10387312 and LINEAR spread for sets containing vanilla village roots; activation is logged at line 18029. This records the hook, not final encounter pacing or freedom from later placement modifiers. Its decoration mixin downgrades one loading error log to debug without adding content.

grouping_decision.name: Moog's Nether Structures Circular Ruin
grouping_decision.rationale: Two circular ruin designs form one working family with distinct biome, material, layout and encounter variants. Definitions differ only in biome constraints and start pools; each reaches one circle template under ruins. Blackstone has a wither skeleton spawner and houses loot references, while nether brick has piglin and piglin brute spawners and no packaged loot references. These differences remain attributed to their individual templates in the joined inventory. Shared circular ruin identity does not imply equivalent hostility, rewards or occupied geometry. Both layouts retain a circular arrangement of upright ruin elements around an encounter space. This arrangement differs from generic fragments and from the broken obsidian portal frame. The cemetery instead uses an organized rectangular grave plot. These design relationships are resolved; effective generation remains unresolved.

Source configs and optional pieces are not live population observations.
mob_source.pool_ownership: Every Small architectural piece uses small_arena_spawners; all six Large architectural pieces use large_arena_pillars; seven Dragon upper pieces use dragon_arena_pillars. Dragon lower platforms and all selected mob pieces use minecraft:empty. mob_any selects Arena Bowman skeleton, Pit Vanguard zombified_piglin and Ember Sentinel blaze at weights 3/3/2. Small additionally selects Pit Brute wither_skeleton, Large Arena Gladiator wither_skeleton, Dragon Drakebone Tyrant wither_skeleton through dedicated receivers.

grouping_decision.name: Moog's Nether Structures Dragon Arena
grouping_decision.rationale: A sculptural dragon encounter assembled from seven upper architectural pieces, thirteen lower platform pieces and four selected mob templates. The inspected head, body and limb forms establish a distinct focal design above a broad platform, rather than another layout of the walled-arena family. Trial spawners, vaults and ordinary spawners remain encounter components, as do shared mob templates. Preserve the fixed-height terrain adaptation and selected 1.21.1 content; template totals are the reachable set, not a claim that every generated instance includes every piece. These membership findings do not establish effective placement, occupied dimensions or actual gameplay.

loot_table_source.basis: Template-owned table refs, processor-configured reward refs and fixed items remain distinct. No rolled reward, repeatability or productive-operation claim.
loot_table_source.fixed_payloads: Dragon c2 /entities/0 is an item frame holding The Dragon's Communion written book. Its lore is not evidence of a living dragon, ritual or working recipe. Saved mob equipment is separately preserved, not a guaranteed drop.
loot_table_source.processor_rewards: Large/Dragon vault processors select mns:vaults/<large_arena or dragon_arena>/main or main_ominous according to the vault block OMINOUS state, replace key_item and clear saved server/shared data. Trial normal/ominous configs explicitly select corresponding mns:spawners/<family>/trial_reward_key or trial_reward_key_ominous tables. See full processor/config entries in mob_source. Raw vault omissions are therefore not effective table omissions.

mob_source.basis: Processor code replaces empty ordinary-spawner NBT, clears trial spawn_data and installs manager-loaded normal/ominous configs. TrialSpawnerConfigManager converts trial_spawner JSON objects to NBT. Raw empty entity objects are not unresolved effective assignments where these selected processors apply. Source configs and optional pieces are not live population observations.
mob_source.pool_ownership: Every Small architectural piece uses small_arena_spawners; all six Large architectural pieces use large_arena_pillars; seven Dragon upper pieces use dragon_arena_pillars. Dragon lower platforms and all selected mob pieces use minecraft:empty. mob_any selects Arena Bowman skeleton, Pit Vanguard zombified_piglin and Ember Sentinel blaze at weights 3/3/2. Small additionally selects Pit Brute wither_skeleton, Large Arena Gladiator wither_skeleton, Dragon Drakebone Tyrant wither_skeleton through dedicated receivers.

grouping_decision.rationale: Two snowy igloo roots form one working family with different layouts, rewards and encounter content. Definitions are identical except start pool. Both reach the same three vanilla snowy-villager templates; these shared entity pieces are not extra structure families or proof of three villagers per igloo. grouping_decision.name: Repurposed Structures Monument

processor_effects.material_replacements: Noise and random replacement callers operate on the configured input block and preserve position/NBT, delegating compatible state-property copying to GeneralUtils. Their selected monument outputs are material changes, not additional direct entity or loot assignments. Exact patterns are not measured.
processor_effects.nether_lava: Selected rules change air to lava under a 0..31 Y-position predicate. YValuePosRuleTest tests its second position argument inclusively. Effective engine argument mapping and predicate registration remain unverified; no converted-block observation is claimed.
processor_effects.pillar_delegation: Extension positions invoke referenced processors through processBlock only. The direct chunk write uses returned state at the extension position and discards returned NBT. It does not invoke delegate finalizeProcessing. Thus the jungle surface archaeology delegate is not applied through this pillar path.
processor_effects.pillar_extension: PillarProcessor matches the complete trigger state and extends along the configured direction within build bounds, strict length distance and its land/replaceability checks. It skips extension outside the WorldGenRegion center chunk. The default length ceiling is 1000, direction DOWN and forced_placement false; selected red-glass columns explicitly force length 2. These are source bounds, not observed heights.
processor_effects.remaining: Engine processing/finalization behavior, effective registry activation, relevant retained modifications, land-helper semantics, generated-world attribution and final geometry remain unresolved.
processor_effects.reproducibility: The surface finalizer uses Collections.shuffle(List) without a supplied seeded random. This establishes a source-level ordering limitation, not an observed world mismatch. Full processor seed determinism is not claimed.
processor_effects.surface_loot: CappedStructureSurfaceProcessor implements finalizeProcessing, requires equal original/processed list sizes, filters to placement bounds and surface eligibility, then invokes its delegate processBlock. It keeps only nonnull changed results in the processed list. The jungle delegate can assign suspicious-gravel archaeology loot on eligible template blocks. Effective engine invocation and placed archaeology blocks remain UNKNOWN.

grouping_decision.rationale: Four material/biome variants share the custom MonumentBuilding room graph and ordered room fitters. Captured building/fitter call sites bind candidate pools and templates. Rooms, openings and body sections are components, not additional families. Nether fixes Y at 30; other variants use terrain weighting, and spawn overrides differ. Exact graph reachability and effective content remain unresolved.

Land variants generally author villagers, domestic animals, cats and iron golems, with zombie-villager templates except mushroom. Mushroom additionally authors mooshroom. Ocean authors drowned. Crimson and warped author piglin, piglin_brute, hoglin, zoglin, zombified_piglin and strider. Item/item_frame are non-mob entities. Tree features with beehive decorators supply an additional potential bee source. No unresolved template entity sources or generation markers; no realized populations inferred.

underground_surface_classification.assessment: Land variants project to WORLD_SURFACE_WG with offset0 and beard_thin; swamp runs at top_layer_modification. Ocean projects to OCEAN_FLOOR_WG with offset0, maxY52, terrain range26/radius2 and biome radius2: seabed/submerged intent. Its path processor declares OCEAN_FLOOR_WG gravity and require_water_surface. Crimson/warped use generic_nether_jigsaw_structure, HIGHEST_LAND offset0 and beard_box: Nether land-associated settlements. Other root differences remain explicit in variants. Saved oak geometry is one family example, not a size bound on every variant; supports and path projection do not prove occupied volume or burial.

visual_discoverability.assessment: Town centers, buildings, connecting paths and farms provide settlement cues. Land designs use biome-related materials and vegetation; giant mushrooms, jungle/swamp trees and terrain can obscure buildings. Ocean uses seabed construction and coral; Nether uses crimson/warped materials. Qualitative cues only, with no measured visibility distance or guaranteed visible entrance.

loot_table_source.fixed_payloads: Main block_entities/35 pulley saves one rope. hull_front02 block_entities/1 urn saves one ash; its armor stand saves a chainmail helmet. hull_room01 block_entities/1 jar saves six cookies in slots0..5 and an empty fluid. These are source payloads, not verified recovery or live loot outcomes.
loot_table_source.processors: remove_disabled_blocks replaces configured-disabled blocks while preserving incoming position/NBT. Frozen cannon, urn, jar, globe, cannonball, ash, candle-holder, gold door/trapdoor/bars and sconce settings are enabled. Sail04 uses empty processors. No invented container loot or block-spawner injection is attributed.
loot_table_source.urn_rewards: Treasure urn block loot refers to urn common/uncommon/rare/epic reward tables with weight/quality60/-5,32/-2,7/2,1/5; silk-touch and treasure-state conditions remain separate. UrnBlock.getDrops appends existing container contents. Reuse the exact tables and conditions recorded for supplementaries:cave_urn_cache and urn-reward-behavior; Galleon selects urns_patch directly without the cave-urn six-origin placement repetition.

mob_source.boats: Boat pool weights1/1/2/1/2 select dark-oak boat with plunderer+pillager, boat with plunderer, cannon_boat with plunderer, unoccupied boat, or empty. Nonempty entries declare attempts4 and spread4. The implementation loops attempts+5, so up to nine candidate attempts; it returns on first successful placement, not nine boats. X/Z offsets are inclusive -4..4. Terrain matching uses WORLD_SURFACE_WG at the feature origin, then requires candidate air, ground-rule acceptance and an available chunk.
mob_source.feature_pool: galleon/plunderer selects plunderer/pillager/empty at weights4/1/1. SpawnEntityWithPassengersFeature creates selected entities, finalizes mobs with STRUCTURE spawn type, conditionally applies its configured persistence and adds the entity with passengers.
mob_source.ordinary_natural: Root spawn_overrides is empty, but the separate named spawn-box declaration must not be discarded. Ordinary biome/world spawning outside special handling remains conditional.
mob_source.saved_entity_details: hull_back03 entities/0 saves ravager Health100, PersistenceRequired1, empty equipment. hull_room02 entities/0 saves iron_golem Health100, PersistenceRequired0, empty equipment. hull_front02 entities/0 saves armor stand Health20 with chainmail helmet. These saved records do not establish successful placement or survival.
mob_source.spawn_box_basis: Four main-template moonlight:spawn_box markers name galleon_enemies. GalleonStructure exposes its SpawnBoxSettings. Moonlight ChunkGeneratorMixin intercepts getMobsAt to request special spawn lists; SpawnBoxStructurePiece resolves a named box containing the queried position. This is a configured regional spawn-list mechanism, not a block spawner or measured recurring population.
mob_source.urn_break_creatures: Treasure urns placed by urns_patch can release an entity on break, subject to the frozen0.01 random check, doTileDrops and no prevents_infested_spawns tool enchantment. Selection uses actual urn_spawn tag holders. Required packaged declarations are silverfish, slime and bat; optional declarations are not asserted available. Reuse urn-reward-behavior evidence.

grouping_decision.name: Towns & Towers Village
grouping_decision.rationale: One settlement family with twenty-six retained architectural and placement variants, consistent with CTOV and Integrated Villages settlement treatment. The shared role is an authored inhabited settlement, not one identical building layout. The trader camp connects a meeting point to tent, llama-pen and authored wandering-trader components. Grove concentrates beds, workstations and villager connectors in one building; snowy slopes supplies an inn with beds, villager connectors and decor. These concentrated settlements and the broader house/street assemblies retain their own full root definitions. Piglin village retains piglin/brute spawn overrides rather than the ordinary empty override; settlement membership does not imply peaceful inhabitants. The separate ocean-village record retains its ship assembly and water placement. Vanilla-ID village replacements and injected buildings stay with their consuming vanilla family; they do not alias these separate Towns and Towers roots. Canonical design relationships are resolved. Missing inhabitant pools and street/house templates remain explicit. Effective generation, occupied geometry, population and remaining gameplay attributes are unproven.

processor_assignment.condition: Processed block is an instance of ChestBlock; barrels are not selected by this test.

processor_assignment.selector: BuildingListFeature.ChestProcessor calls LootTableUtil.getTable on the noise biome at the processed block position (coordinates shifted right by 2).

betterend:biome_ruins.mechanism: Active biome building lists independently select these 35 complete ruin-named templates. Canonical assignments follow inspected block arrangements and stored content.
betterend:biome_ruins.relationship: Ten ruin design families account for thirty templates; five fixture templates contribute no family. Cross-biome material swaps, differing survival/damage, orientations and furnishings remain explicit template variants. These are interpretive architectural groupings, not claims that every variant is a transformed copy or that an original intact building can be reconstructed.
betterend:biome_ruins.scope: Membership of this selected template set is resolved. Cube diagrams assist layout comparison but do not model partial block geometry or establish generated-world placement. Per-template contents and dimensions are retained for required attribute work; no loot, hostility or measured-footprint acceptance is implied.

dispositions.rationale: Preserve this named architectural candidate but do not add it to active families. Neither packaging nor the adjacent legacy structures.json supplies an active route through the current configured lists.

betterend:blossoming_spires/house.mechanism: A furnished house template is packaged outside all six active configured building lists. The direct consumer loads the selected path without scanning adjacent files.
betterend:blossoming_spires/house.scope: This is the established BetterEnd building-list consumer boundary, not a claim that manually placing the house is impossible. A demonstrated additional consumer would reopen eligibility. No baseline resource is changed.

approximate_footprint.basis: Selected vanilla template dimensions; rotation can exchange axes. Placement intersects the template box with makeBox.
approximate_footprint.erosion_scope: StructureErode.erodeIntense may relocate block states to floor(x+2*nextGaussian()+0.5), likewise Z. This path has no explicit finite horizontal clamp, so the nominal hull is not a bound on all scattered debris. No observed occupied footprint is claimed.

approximate_vertical_size.basis: Selected vanilla template height before erosion. getYOffset passes height>>3 and height>>2 (3 and 6) to MHelper.randRange and negates the result; place applies Java integer conversion after adding 0.5.
approximate_vertical_size.erosion_scope: Erosion and drop search down toward the intersected box minimum Y minus 10 and may place displaced blocks outside the hull height. This is not exposed height or a strict total debris bound.

authored_or_natural_enemies.basis: IgnoreEntities=true, filtered Sentry markers and no custom mob creation. Do not copy End-city encounters merely because the hull template is shared.
authored_or_natural_enemies.value: No direct authored enemies from the ship template/marker path; natural enemies may occur.

Twenty-seven packaged BetterEnd biomes reference it directly; twenty-one occur in the captured End biome source. This establishes a natural-generation route, not observed occurrence or exploration frequency.

dimension.basis: The placed definition applies rarity 500, in-square and biome filters. Twenty-seven packaged BetterEnd biomes reference it directly; twenty-one occur in the captured End biome source. This establishes a natural-generation route, not observed occurrence or exploration frequency.
dimension.limitation: Captured biome-source overlap and packaged route, not observed occurrence.

generated_spawners.processor_behavior: CrashedShipFeature$1 replaces Blocks.SPAWNER with AIR and null NBT. Erosion does not create a spawner or spawner NBT.
generated_spawners.scope: Template and generator contribution; surrounding pre-existing blocks are not inventoried as authored ship contents.

intended_hostility.basis: Structure/air markers are ignored and template entities disabled. No EndCityPiece marker handler is called. The replacer converts spawners and wool-sound blocks to air; erosion handles block states.
intended_hostility.value: Abandoned wreck without the vanilla End-city authored defenders.

loot_table_source.elytra: Elytra marker is ignored; this feature does not call the vanilla marker handler that creates the item frame/reward.
loot_table_source.fixed_contents: The brewing stand contains two saved minecraft:potion stacks with minecraft:strong_healing potion components, slots 0 and 2. These are fixed template contents, not loot-table rolls.
loot_table_source.scope: Source attribution. Placement and erosion can remove or alter blocks; no guaranteed surviving chest, potion reward, dragon head or elytra is asserted.
loot_table_source.template_chests: Two saved chest compounds have Items=[] and no LootTable. Chest markers are ignored; no vanilla End-city chest table assignment is invoked.

mob_source.basis: Selected template entity list is empty, placement ignores entities and Sentry data markers are filtered rather than processed by EndCityPiece. Erosion removes/relocates block states, with no direct entity creation.
mob_source.natural_source: Natural biome mobs and surrounding world conditions remain separate; no live encounter is claimed.

underground_surface_classification.basis: Origin is moved to chunk center at Y=128 before getGround. Requires selected ground Y>5 and END_STONES below. canSpawn computes both distance terms from chunk X, accepting 2*(X>>4)^2>=3600, not a radial X/Z exclusion. Rotation/mirror and negative template-height-derived offset are applied; no terrain merge is selected.
underground_surface_classification.value: Grounded, partly lowered wreck with erosion.

visual_discoverability.basis: Source-derived form, not measured approach visibility or discovery distance.
visual_discoverability.source_form: Standalone eroded wreck made from the vanilla End-city ship template; rotation and erosion vary its surviving silhouette.

betterend:crashed_ship.configured_feature: Inline configuration; no separate configured-feature registry ID.
betterend:crashed_ship.mechanism: Registered placed feature with inline betterend:crashed_ship configuration, directly consumed by packaged End biomes.
betterend:crashed_ship.placement_eligibility: The placed definition applies rarity 500, in-square and biome filters. Twenty-seven packaged BetterEnd biomes reference it directly; twenty-one occur in the captured End biome source. This establishes a natural-generation route, not observed occurrence or exploration frequency.
betterend:crashed_ship.relationship: One independent crashed-ship family. It reuses the vanilla End-city ship template, but its own placement and erosion generate a standalone wreck. The ship attached to minecraft:end_city remains a component of that city family. Rotation, erosion and biome occurrences do not create additional crashed-ship families.
betterend:crashed_ship.scope: Family membership resolved from existing source and active placement eligibility. Complete provider coverage and required family attributes remain open. Shared biome modifiers may extend eligibility but do not add a second family for this same generator.

dispositions.rationale: The template is an individual light fixture, with no separate building, platform or composed site. A template boundary and the use of a building-list generator do not make it a structure family.

betterend:lantern_woods/light_1.mechanism: A narrow pedestal/wall/fence support carries a chain and filalux light. It is selected by the active Lantern Woods building list.
betterend:lantern_woods/light_1.scope: The fixture remains enabled and attributable. This excludes its membership only, not the other independently assembled Lantern Woods buildings.

approximate_footprint.basis: Both radii are equal. Fallen writer selects radius with randRange(2,4); basement uses randRange(2,5). These are parent-cylinder diameters before rotation, displacement, subtraction and voxelization.
approximate_footprint.scope: Approximate source geometry, not occupied-world bounds. Fallen displaces its cylinder; basement subtracts a displaced plane. Do not claim a fixed rectangular footprint.
approximate_footprint.world_space_interpretation: For parent axial length L, radius r and tilt theta about a horizontal axis, horizontal span along the tilt direction is L*abs(sin(theta))+2*r*abs(cos(theta)); transverse span is 2*r. Random azimuth changes X/Z projections.

approximate_vertical_size.basis: Both writers pass L/2 to SDFCappedCone.setHeight. Captured getDistance uses abs(y)-height and twice-height in its side segment, establishing a centered half-height convention.
approximate_vertical_size.nominal_parent_vertical_span: L*abs(cos(theta))+2*r*abs(sin(theta)) before weathering/subtraction and voxelization. Translation changes altitude, not span.

rotation_parameters.betterend:fallen_pillar: theta=pi+0.05*nextGaussian(), about a random horizontal axis. Near pi reverses the axis; the name does not prove a horizontal fallen log.

The captured empty-list constructor and codec/dispatcher therefore expose no supported direct callback modifying the selected End features.

fabric_dispatch_resolution.finding: BiomeModificationImpl constructs an empty modifier list. addModifier appends caller-supplied phase, selector and callback records. FabricBiomeModifier.modify applies records only for their matching phase and biome predicate. It performs no unconditional feature insertion or removal itself.
fabric_dispatch_resolution.remaining: Resolved for the frozen packaged direct-consumer path; no further dispatcher tracing is required.

effective_biome_gap.finding: These retained NeoForge biome-modifier documents name code-backed modifier types without declaring target biomes or feature changes. Their documents cannot prove either removal or preservation of the packaged End feature lists.
effective_biome_gap.required_followup: Resolve relevant registrations and callbacks for these two implementations before asserting that the packaged biome feature membership is effective. Reuse existing source extraction; do not infer modifications from provider names alone.
effective_biome_gap.scope: Concrete unresolved code-delegation paths found in the packaged catalog. This is not a claim that these modifiers alter End features or an exhaustive list of all cross-provider effects.

zeta_resolution.biome_predicate: CompoundBiomeConfig rejects null and requires both component predicates. BiomeTagConfig passes a non-null holder when any tag matches XOR isBlacklist, so an empty blacklist passes. StrictBiomeConfig compares a registered key location string with biomeStrings XOR isBlacklist; its direct-Biome lambda returns false. SpiralSpiresModule defaults therefore admit minecraft:end_highlands only. Frozen configuration records the same empty tag blacklist and named-biome allowlist. Spiral Spires field binding is resolved in spire_configuration_binding.
zeta_resolution.execution_chain: DeferredFeature.place calls WorldGenHandler.generateChunk with its stored stage. The handler requires WorldGenRegion, an enabled consumer module and Generator.canGenerate. That inherited method evaluates its condition and passes accessor.getLevel() to DimensionConfig, resolving the Level-versus-WorldGenRegion ambiguity. Generator.generate then dispatches to MultiChunkFeatureGenerator.generateChunk for these two Quark consumers.
zeta_resolution.modifier_effect: During ADD, ZetaBiomeModifier appends a deferred feature at each decoration stage. The captured method does not remove the existing feature list. It separately delegates spawn configuration to ZetaSpawnModifier.
zeta_resolution.remaining: Spiral Spires generation-setting binding is resolved by the linked source, frozen file and initial-refresh log. Other Quark consumer settings, actual spawn registrations and Forgified Fabric callbacks remain unresolved. The selected consumers do not establish complete retained-provider coverage.
zeta_resolution.scope: Resolved direct source call chain and preserved frozen-file values. No runtime field dump, observed generation, new canonical family or unconditional central-island exclusion is claimed.

selected_consumers.ChorusVegetationModule: Registers ChorusVegetationGenerator at VEGETAL_DECORATION with weight zero. Its source query excludes positions closer than 1050 to origin and requires END_HIGHLANDS at maxBuildHeight-1. It places chorus vegetation rather than authored template structures.
selected_consumers.SpiralSpiresModule: Registers SpiralSpireGenerator at SURFACE_STRUCTURES with weight zero, supplying its dimension configuration. Its source query excludes positions closer than 1050 to origin. Chunk-part generation checks the configured biome predicate and searches for End Stone before block-level spire construction.

zeta_resolution.source_reach: MultiChunkFeatureGenerator searches source chunks within ceil(radius/16) of the target on both axes, using source chunk minimum X/Z and Y=0. This is source search reach, not occupied-block geometry. At radii 7 and 15, both search one neighboring chunk per axis.

spiral_spire_geometry.body: For y=-5 through H-1, skip a negative layer when its central block cannot occlude. Otherwise r=ceil(abs((pi/2-atan((max(0,y)+0.5)/(H/a)))*4)). Iterate X/Z offsets -r+1 through r-1, retaining offsets with x*x+z*z<=r*r. At the square-edge offsets, nextFloat()<0.2 selects NewStoneTypesModule.myaliteBlock; all other body positions use dusky_myalite. Writes use flag 2 and discard success.
spiral_spire_geometry.classification_scope: One working geological-landmark family is retained as quark:spiral_spire. Procedural construction rather than a template does not exclude a recognizable landmark design. Random height, taper, crystal winding and repeated spires remain variants or instances. This is an Item 8 identity decision, not an Item 9 tier.
spiral_spire_geometry.conservative_envelope: Body r<=7, hence body X/Z offsets are within -6..6. Since i<=1089 and radialGrowth<0.16, crystal X/Z integer offsets are within -17..17. Crystal Y<=69+round(1089*0.2/10)=91; body Y>=-5. Thus all requested makeSpike writes fit a conservative 35x97x35 XYZ box relative to the anchor, including empty space. This is an analytic upper envelope, not a typical footprint, an attained maximum or a measured world extent.
spiral_spire_geometry.content: The captured generator directly writes Myalite-related blocks. It does not load templates, assign loot tables, configure physical spawners or request entities. Block behavior, later interactions, ordinary drops and other providers remain separate.
spiral_spire_geometry.crystal_spiral: Choose N=(80+nextInt(30))*10, angle magnitude 0.12+nextDouble()*0.16 with random sign, radial growth 0.12+nextDouble()*0.04, and vertical growth nextDouble()*0.2. For i=0..N-1, X/Z are Java-truncated sin/cos(i*angle/10)*i*radialGrowth/10; Y is H+round(i*verticalGrowth/10). Request myalite_crystal at those offsets. Placement probability is one until a chosen cutoff in [0.5*N,0.8*N), then decreases linearly. Repeated rounded positions and discarded write results prevent treating iteration count as occupied blocks.
spiral_spire_geometry.preflight: makeSpike chooses H=50+nextInt(20), so H is 50..69, and taper parameter a=5+nextDouble(). It checks the central column from originY-5 through originY+H-1, accepting only air, End Stone, crying obsidian, obsidian or the module myalite_crystal block. Any other central-column block returns before construction. This is not a clearance check of the entire footprint.

approximate_footprint.arena_derivation: Spike centers are floor(42*cos(angle)), floor(42*sin(angle)), each within -42..42. Each 19-wide component centered with pivot (9,0,9) extends nine blocks in each horizontal direction, so the ring fits -51..51 on both axes, or 103 by 103. The central 29-wide podium fits inside that horizontal bound. Conservative nominal envelope including air, not occupied geometry or exact tight bounds.

families.placement_interpretation: The selected end_spike placed feature has only a biome filter; configured spikes is empty and crystal_invulnerable is false. Actual custom spike layout, top/bottom offsets and respawn invocation are recorded in spike_podium_generators. The placed-feature filter does not constrain the separately captured dragon-fight lifecycle calls.
families.rationale: The ring of spikes and central podium form one dragon-fight arena. Initial generation, dragon death and respawn coordinate their creation or rebuilding through the captured dragon-fight lifecycle. Spike tops/bottoms and podium sections are components; initial, guarded, broken and open forms are state or design variants. Ten spike positions are instances within the arena, not ten families.

betterendisland:platform_gateway.family_scope: Three working authored-design families cover the linked packaged templates exactly once. This is a grouping decision from the captured invocation and lifecycle relationships, not a claim of three newly registered structures. Required attributes and cross-provider reconciliation remain incomplete.
betterendisland:platform_gateway.gateway_placement: Subtract integer half template X/Y/Z from context origin. Use context random, Rotation.NONE, pivot (1,0,1), IGNORE_WATERLOGGING and placement flag 2. After the template call, request END_GATEWAY at context origin with flag 3, regardless of the template helper result. If configuration has an exit and the block entity is an EndGateway, set its exit position/exactness and mark changed.

generated_world_observations.attribution: Material presence is consistent with the linked spike templates, but this projection does not preserve individual block positions or establish exclusive provider ownership. Exact template/variant attribution remains UNKNOWN. No podium, gateway or spawn-platform generation is claimed from these counts.

Absence of block entities here is not proof that a provider cannot place them elsewhere or on another lifecycle event.
generated_world_observations.observation: Saved sections contain obsidian, End Stone bricks, End Stone brick walls and End Stone brick slabs. The selected chunk records contain no block entities. These are actual decoded block-state counts, not unused palette names.
generated_world_observations.scope: Accepted Item 7 ordinary seed 42 run-a, minecraft:the_end, block X/Z -64 through 63. Offline extraction of manifest-verified saved regions; no new generation or survey.

betterendisland:platform_gateway.hooks: Both inject at HEAD and are cancellable. With useVanillaSpawnPlatform false, the platform hook invokes the custom generator, discards its boolean and cancels vanilla execution. With useVanillaEndGateways false, the gateway hook returns the custom generator boolean. True leaves the respective vanilla path alone.

Common.init assigns betterEnd from the platform helper using mod ID betterend. The preserved runtime loading/configuration evidence and derived betterEnd=true branch are linked below.

The packaged service declarations name NeoForgePlatformHelper and NeoForgeModulesLoader respectively. NeoForgePlatformHelper.isModLoaded delegates to ModList.get().isLoaded(id). NeoForgeModulesLoader delegates to the IModulesLoader default method; no behavior is inferred here for that unexamined default.

betterendisland:platform_gateway.mechanism: Conditional mixin replacements of vanilla EndPlatformFeature.createEndPlatform and EndGatewayFeature.place, not additional structure-registry roots.

betterendisland:platform_gateway.packaged_template_content: Both linked templates have empty entities and block_entities. This excludes neither processor-created blocks nor the gateway block explicitly placed by code.
betterendisland:platform_gateway.platform_placement: Offset the input position down 14 blocks, then subtract integer half template X/Z. Use Rotation.NONE, pivot (3,0,3), IGNORE_WATERLOGGING and placement flag 2. A fresh RandomSource.create() is used rather than a supplied seeded source. The destroyBlocks boolean is forwarded to placeTemplate but not read there.

processor_effects.DragonEggProcessor: Reads the existing world block at the incoming target position. If it is DRAGON_EGG, replaces the incoming block state with default DRAGON_EGG while preserving position and incoming NBT. Otherwise returns the incoming block unchanged. This preserves an existing egg, rather than creating an egg reward at an empty target.
processor_effects.ObsidianProcessor: Only incoming OBSIDIAN is transformed. Obtain random from StructurePlaceSettings.getRandom(target position); clamp dragon kills to 0..10; use lerp(clampedKills/10.0, 0, 0.5) as the nextFloat threshold for CRYING_OBSIDIAN, otherwise default OBSIDIAN. Preserve position and incoming NBT. Non-obsidian input passes through unchanged.
processor_effects.scope: Direct block substitution only. Neither processor directly spawns entities, configures spawners or assigns loot tables. This does not establish engine/API behavior, ordinary block drops, external retained-stack modifications or observed world results.

betterendisland:platform_gateway.processors: Platform static processor list is empty; gateway static list contains DragonEggProcessor. Both then add ObsidianProcessor with dragon-kill count, read only when the supplied accessor is a ServerLevel with a non-null dragon fight, otherwise zero. Direct effects are recorded below.

runtime_activation.better_end_derivation: Combining the recorded betterend mod/container and selected NeoForgePlatformHelper with the captured Common.init assignment and ModList.isLoaded delegation gives betterEnd=true for this stack initialization. Therefore the recorded spike top-anchor branch is Y=70 and loader radius is 42. This is a derivation from runtime loading plus preserved code, not a direct field dump or measured occupied-world extent.
runtime_activation.finding: The preserved runtime log records both mods in the mod list and creates their containers, records the two actual NeoForge service selections, applies the six directly relevant mixins and loads the Better End Island configuration. The captured configuration bytes match the frozen file exactly. This resolves runtime mixin/service activation and configuration-file identity for registry-r1.
runtime_activation.limitations: Log application records do not prove each generation hook executed or placed a template successfully. No arena, gateway, platform or respawn observation is inferred from readiness or class transformation. Generated-world reconciliation remains open.

betterendisland:platform_gateway.scope: Source, packaged template and registry-r1 runtime activation attribution. Family reconciliation, dimension applicability and generated-world observations remain open.

spike_podium_generators.podium_entity_source: When isInitialSpawn is true, after the template helper, request four EndCrystal entities, one eight blocks in each horizontal cardinal direction from origin.above(6), with X/Z centered by +0.5. Set showBottom false and invulnerable true. This branch does not check template-helper success and discards entity-add results. It establishes direct authored entity requests, not successful observed generation or hostile-mob spawning.
spike_podium_generators.podium_geometry: Use context origin and random, subtract integer half template X/Z, Rotation.NONE, and pivot (3,0,3) for bottom-only or (14,0,14) otherwise. Full tower envelope is 29x27x29; bottom-only is 7x11x7. These include air and are not occupied-block measurements.

podium_invocation.arguments: The helper arguments after fight/level are isActive, isBottomOnly and a vanilla-branch crystal-suppression flag. The two-boolean overload supplies false for the last flag. The custom constructor receives (fight.isFirstExitPortalSpawn(), isBottomOnly, isActive), and placement uses portalLocation.below(5), FeatureConfiguration.NONE, level chunk generator and a fresh RandomSource.create(). Placement boolean is discarded.
podium_invocation.configuration: ExitPortalUtils.spawnPortal selects spawnCentralTowerOnResummon when hasDragonEverSpawned is true, otherwise spawnCentralTowerInitially. Both frozen values are true, selecting BetterEndPodiumFeature in either state when the bound configuration applies. The vanilla branch is consequently not selected by these frozen values.
podium_invocation.dragon_death: For the tracked dragon UUID, setDragonKilled always calls spawnPortal(true,true). Its preceding full-tower call requires zero prior kills, spawnCentralTowerInitially false and spawnCentralTowerOnResummon true, so that preceding branch is disabled by the frozen true/true tower settings.
podium_invocation.initial_scan: EndDragonFightMixin.scanForInitialState calls spawnPortal(false,false) when no active exit portal exists and findExitPortal is null. This requests a full inactive tower; first-exit flag determines initial versus broken template. The mixin constructor initializes that flag true; persisted/restored state applicability remains separate.
podium_invocation.missing_portal_recovery: EndDragonFightMixin.spawnDragon calls spawnPortal(false,false) then spawnPortal(true,true) if portalLocation is null and findExitPortal returns null. This requests a full inactive tower followed by an active bottom-only portal. The first helper clears the first-exit flag before the second call.
podium_invocation.origin_adjustment: ExitPortalUtils retains a non-null portalLocation with Y >= 5. Otherwise it requests WorldgenUtils.getSurfacePosAt(level,0,0), descends while the block is bedrock and Y exceeds sea level, and falls back to (0,65,0) if Y remains below 5. It updates portalLocation before placement. WorldgenUtils.getSurfacePosAt scans downward from getMaxBuildHeight while Y > getMinBuildHeight and returns the first END_STONE block Y, not the highest arbitrary solid block. It returns -1 if no match, causing the recorded Y=65 fallback.
podium_invocation.reset: The reset method sets first-exit false, then directly constructs BetterEndPodiumFeature(true,false,false) when spawnCentralTowerInitially is true. It places at portalLocation.below(5) with a fresh random source and discards the result. The direct constructor flag therefore selects an initial full tower regardless of the reset first-exit field.
podium_invocation.scope: Direct source and frozen-value derivation for the captured callers, including respawn calls below. Effective runtime execution and generated-world observations remain to be reconciled. This does not add a family or imply complete provider coverage.
podium_invocation.success_limits: spawnPortal returns void and sets first-exit false after the placement branch, even if the custom feature returned false. A call proves neither template placement nor successful entity insertion. Exceptions can prevent reaching the final flag update.

spike_podium_generators.podium_variants: Constructor arguments are isInitialSpawn, isBottomOnly, isActive, in that order. Bottom-only selects betterendisland:tower_bottom_open; otherwise initial selects betterendisland:tower_initial and false selects betterendisland:tower_broken. The invocation mapping and frozen tower switches are resolved below; successful runtime placement is not inferred.
spike_podium_generators.processors: Spike static order: three BlockReplaceProcessor instances (orange terracotta selector with obsidian/crying obsidian; magenta terracotta selector with air/crying obsidian/obsidian; purple concrete selector with obsidian), then DragonEggProcessor, then per-placement ObsidianProcessor. Podium: gray concrete/bedrock BlockReplaceProcessor, DragonEggProcessor, active red concrete/end portal or inactive red concrete/air BlockReplaceProcessor, then ObsidianProcessor. For these instances all four optional flags are false. BlockReplaceProcessor matches incoming block type, selects output with settings random at target position, preserves incoming position/NBT and passes nonmatching input unchanged. No optional property copying, facing/half randomization or waterlog preservation applies. Configured outputs exclude water/lava, so its fluid-tick branch does not apply. Selector arguments are not asserted as observed frequencies.

respawn_generation.dragon_source: END.onStart clears the custom stage, sets dragonKilled false and invokes EndDragonFightAccessor.invokeCreateNewDragon. This is a direct authored dragon creation request associated with the arena, separate from stored template entities or a spawner. Successful entity creation remains a runtime claim.
respawn_generation.other_material_changes: END.onStart also conditionally replaces existing OBSIDIAN with CRYING_OBSIDIAN using threshold lerp(clamp(dragon kills,0,10)/10,0,0.5). It covers gateway positions for indices 0..19 absent from the remaining-gateways list and a fixed box around END_SPAWN_POINT. These are changes to existing blocks, not new gateway or platform family creation. Block-update results are discarded.
respawn_generation.pillar_clearance: The rebuild requests a strength-5 BLOCK-interaction explosion at spike center plus 0.5 X/Z and base Y plus crystal offset minus 1. It then removes non-END_STONE blocks in the inclusive X/Z center +/-11 and Y EndSpike.height +/-40 when betterEnd, otherwise +/-30 box. This affects existing blocks; it is not an additional authored family or an observed destruction measurement.
respawn_generation.pillar_rebuild: SUMMONING_PILLARS processes the spike indexed by integer tick/40 when tick modulo 40 is 0 or 39. At 0 it redirects supplied crystal beams; at 39 it requests an explosion and block clearing, then Feature.END_SPIKE.place with SpikeConfiguration(true, singleton spike, beam target (0,128,0)), level chunk generator, fresh random and origin (centerX,45,centerZ). It discards placement success. The captured SpikeFeatureMixin routes this ServerLevel call through the non-WorldGenRegion branch, selecting guarded/broken templates and requesting a crystal.
respawn_generation.podium_rebuild: END.onStart calls spawnPortal(false,false,true), requesting a full inactive podium. If hasDragonEverSpawned was already true, it subsequently calls spawnPortal(false,true,true), requesting an inactive bottom-only podium. Both frozen tower flags are true; the last helper argument only suppresses crystals in its unselected vanilla branch. The first-exit flag still determines initial/broken full template. At the end, setHasDragonEverSpawned(true).
respawn_generation.scope: Recorded source-level generation effects of SUMMONING_PILLARS and END. No new family, observed frequency, successful respawn or completed runtime coverage is asserted. Other phases and external interactions are not exhaustively characterized by this record.
respawn_generation.stage_binding: DragonRespawnStage static initialization binds class $3 to SUMMONING_PILLARS and class $5 to END. These are phases of one dragon-fight generation path, not separate structure families.

spike_podium_generators.scope: Partial attribution from the preserved full generators. Does not establish final families, complete generated contents, absence of loot/spawners, runtime activation or world observations. Resolve only dependencies needed for those Item 8 attributes.
spike_podium_generators.spike_entity_source: After both template helpers return true, and only when the WorldGenRegion flag is false, request an END_CRYSTAL at (center X + 0.5, anchor Y + IEndSpike crystal offset, center Z + 0.5). Beam target and invulnerability come from SpikeConfiguration. Request BEDROCK one block below. Entity-add and block-write booleans are discarded. EndSpikeMixin supplies the recorded crystal offsets; this is a direct entity request, not a spawner or observed successful spawn.
spike_podium_generators.spike_geometry: Top anchor is (spike center X, 70 when BetterEndIslandCommon.betterEnd is true, otherwise 60, spike center Z); bottom anchor is 67 blocks below. Both subtract integer half template X/Z and use the same random rotation with pivot (9,0,9). Each top template envelope is 19x69x19 and each bottom is 19x67x19. Adjacent vertical anchors give a combined 19x136x19 nominal envelope per spike, including air, not occupied-block height. The runtime/source derivation below selects betterEnd=true, top Y=70; this is not an occupied-world measurement.
spike_podium_generators.spike_hook: SpikeFeatureMixin replaces getSpikesForLevel with the custom result. Its cancellable HEAD placeSpike hook calls BetterSpikeFeature with an accessor-is-WorldGenRegion flag, then cancels vanilla. Neither hook has a local configuration condition.
spike_podium_generators.spike_layout: SpikeCacheLoader places ten centers around radius 42 when betterEnd is true, otherwise 54, using floor(radius*cos(angle)) and floor(radius*sin(angle)), angle 2*(-pi + pi*i/10), i=0..9. BetterEndIslandCommon.init assigns betterEnd from Services.PLATFORM.isModLoaded("betterend"). The runtime/source derivation below selects the true branch (radius 42).
spike_podium_generators.spike_variants: SpikeCacheLoader shuffles 0..9 and creates ten spikes with height 76 + 3*j. chooseTemplates maps (height - 73)/3 to 1..10, then remaps 10 to 9: indices 1..8 once and 9 twice per generated list. Templates are betterendisland:pillar_{initial|guarded|broken}_{index} and betterendisland:pillar_bottom_{index}. WorldGenRegion selects initial; otherwise random nextFloat below 0.2 selects guarded, else broken. The loader guarded flag (j equals 1 or 2) is not consulted by chooseTemplates. This describes the captured loader path, not arbitrary externally supplied EndSpike objects.
spike_podium_generators.success_limits: Both template helpers warn and return false when the template is absent; otherwise they discard StructureTemplate.placeInWorld boolean and return true. Both use IGNORE_WATERLOGGING and flag 2. A false spike helper logs an error and returns before subsequent steps. Podium returns its helper boolean even though initial crystal requests can occur after helper failure.
spike_podium_generators.template_content_scope: These 39 spike/podium templates plus the two previously linked platform/gateway templates account for every template in this provider catalog. All have empty stored entities; only the two full tower templates have block entities (one bell each). This does not erase the direct code-created crystal source or establish complete runtime provider coverage.

betterendisland:platform_gateway.success_limits: Missing templates log a warning and return false. Loaded-template helpers discard placeInWorld boolean and return true. Platform hook cancellation does not depend on success. Gateway returns its template helper result, not whether portal-block placement or exit initialization succeeded.

approximate_footprint.basis: n=2+nextInt(3). Cube loops 0..n inclusive; terrain loops -3..n+3 inclusive on X/Z. The outer corner exclusions do not expand these envelopes.
approximate_footprint.scope: Source write envelopes; conditional terrain changes are not a fully occupied footprint.

approximate_vertical_size.basis: Cube origin offset o=nextInt(4), cube writes Y=o..o+n. Terrain loop writes candidate offsets Y=4 down through -127 (strictly greater than -128). Combined envelope is -127..max(4,o+n), inclusive, or 132..135 blocks.
approximate_vertical_size.scope: Includes deep conditional terrain processing, not visible landmark height. World bounds and predicates can reject writes; the cube itself is only 3..5 blocks tall.

flower_delegate.content: The delegated feature performs plant-state placement, not entity creation, loot-table assignment or spawner configuration. Packaged state inputs include flowers, grasses and shrubs, including wither rose; environmental block hazards do not constitute an authored enemy population. Later plant interactions and ambient natural populations are separate.
flower_delegate.geometry: BlockPredicateFilter tests the current position. SimpleBlockFeature obtains one state, requires canSurvive, and writes at that origin or invokes DoublePlantBlock.placeAt after checking the block above is empty. The latter adds an upper half one block above; no horizontal offset is added. Fairy Ring floor search permits the flower origin through anchor+6, hence a double plant can reach anchor+7. With the buried ore lower bound -45, the combined nominal envelope is 7x53x7.
flower_delegate.limitations: Source-derived requested envelope and packaged delegate possibilities. Failed placement can leave air for subsequent ring-state copies; no completed visible ring, actual flower choice or measured frequency is asserted.
flower_delegate.packaged_scope: All 76 minecraft:flower objects across the retained packaged catalog use an inline minecraft:simple_block delegate with one block_predicate_filter and no other placement modifier. This whole-catalog set is a conservative superset of eligible biome choices, not a claim that every flower can occur in every biome.
flower_delegate.selection: BiomeGenerationSettings builds its flower list by Feature.FLOWER identity. FairyRingGenerator chooses a configured flower, extracts RandomPatchConfiguration.feature(), and calls that inner placed feature rather than the outer patch. The outer tries/xz_spread/y_spread therefore do not expand the ring. An empty list uses oxeye daisy.

Granite, diorite and andesite use the same cluster writer. These are terrain material contributions; registration alone does not establish that the experimental module is enabled.

The additional ore path writes only the supplied stone default state where its matcher accepts existing terrain. Neither the inspected cluster writer nor the ore writer authors rooms, entities, spawners or container loot.

quark:stone_generation.mechanism: BigStoneClustersModule and VanillaStoneClustersModule register BigStoneClusterGenerator at UNDERGROUND_DECORATION. NewStoneTypesModule additionally registers OreGenerator at UNDERGROUND_ORES.
quark:stone_generation.remaining: Effective enablement, frequency, exact occupied extent and world occurrence are not established by this boundary disposition. Candidate enumeration is not claimed exhaustively inspected.
quark:stone_generation.scope: Canonical membership exclusion settled. Existing source-derived content details and limitations remain preserved; no Item 9 classification or claim of observed absence.

dispositions.rationale: Style decorates existing floor/ceiling surfaces with crystals and replaces qualifying walls with stone. Its floor override does not invoke the AIR base writer; mimicInside is false. No authored room, entity, spawner or container-loot operation in the inspected style path.

Style replaces qualifying floor/ceiling/wall/interior terrain and adds occasional short pillars above existing floors. These are terrain materials and decoration variants, not independently authored sites. No entity, spawner or container-loot operation in the inspected style path.

quark:underground_styles.mechanism: CorundumModule and PermafrostModule register UndergroundStyleGenerator at UNDERGROUND_DECORATION, weight one, with their own generationSettings and style names.
quark:underground_styles.remaining: Exact effective tags/configuration, affected area and observed occurrence are not established by this source disposition. quark:underground_styles.scope: Canonical membership exclusion settled. Existing source-derived content details and limitations remain preserved; no Item 9 classification or claim of observed absence.

dispositions.rationale: The generator delegates to Feature.TREE. Selected blue, lavender, orange, red and yellow blossom definitions are minecraft:tree with fancy trunk and foliage placers and empty decorators. These are tree variants, not independently authored structure sites.

The direct generator places leaf carpet or petal patches over water, conditional on configuration and module dependencies. No authored room, entity, spawner or container-loot placement occurs in this path.

dispositions.rationale: The six material and length variants depict fallen vegetation, without an independent constructed site. Stump, log, decorations and each placement selector are not separate families.

regions_unexplored:fallen_tree.mechanism: RUFallenTreeFeature places a stump, then conditionally places a horizontal log run and its attached decoration using six supplied configurations.
regions_unexplored:fallen_tree.scope: The generator can return success after placing only a stump when the full fallen log cannot fit. Retain this limitation and all eight placed variants. Ashen remains a vanilla trial-chamber component, not an additional family.

approximate_footprint.basis: RandomPatchFeature.place offsets each horizontal axis by nextInt(xzSpread+1)-nextInt(xzSpread+1); xz_spread=4 gives -4..4. Nine tries sample this envelope, not a solid footprint. Six placement repetitions can have separate origins; no fixed combined cache outline is claimed.
approximate_footprint.value: Per patch, candidate block positions span at most 9 by 9 blocks; individual urn occupies one block position.

approximate_vertical_size.basis: y_spread=1 gives nextInt(2)-nextInt(2), hence -1..1 from the patch origin. Supported-air predicate filters attempts. FallingUrnEntity permits later displacement; this is initial placement geometry, not a persistent bound.
approximate_vertical_size.value: Per patch, candidate positions span at most 3 block layers; individual urn is one block position tall.

authored_or_natural_enemies.basis: Feature supplies blocks only; the explicit entity source is UrnBlock.spawnAfterBreak. No resident population or natural spawn rate is inferred.
authored_or_natural_enemies.value: Break-triggered creature selection is authored block behavior; ambient cave inhabitants are natural and not supplied by the cache placement.

biome_constraints.basis: ModServerDynamicResources Forge branch publishes HAS_CAVE_URNS with IS_OVERWORLD if URN_PILE_ENABLED. CommonConfigs$Functional binds functional.urn.cave_urns, true in frozen config; functional.urn.enabled is also true. ModTags binds has_cave_urns; generated_pack is enabled in runtime world-context. This is source-derived eligibility, not a direct runtime tag dump.

dimension.basis: Dynamic HAS_CAVE_URNS includes #minecraft:is_overworld when functional.urn.cave_urns is true. Resolved biome overlap with captured dimension sources, not observed occurrence.

generated_spawners.basis: Random patch delegates to simple_block with sole urn state; UrnBlock uses direct conditional entity creation after break, not a spawner block or preplaced mob.
generated_spawners.value: No physical spawner is supplied by this feature.

intended_hostility.basis: Treasure urn loot pool and UrnBlock.spawnAfterBreak; configured critter check is 0.01, subject to block-drop and enchantment conditions. Creature tag includes hostile and nonhostile types; no measured difficulty or encounter rate is asserted.
intended_hostility.value: Treasure cache with conditional break-triggered creature hazard, not an authored resident combat encounter.

loot_table_source.basis: Block table has independent silk-touch urn-item and treasure-state loot pools. Tier entries have weight/quality pairs common 60/-5, uncommon 32/-2, rare 7/2, epic 1/5; conditions and luck affect rewards. Some leaf entries require feature flags. UrnBlock.getDrops delegates to base block drops and appends stored container items when a tile is available. FallingUrnEntity.shatter calls Block.dropResources with an empty tool and reconstructed tile data when present. Source attribution does not promise a realized item or successful drop.
loot_table_source.value: supplementaries:blocks/urn, treasure pool -> supplementaries:loot/urn_loot/urn_loot -> common, uncommon, rare or epic tables.

mob_source.basis: Packaged urn_spawn tag has replace=false. Optional declarations are not asserted present. ModTags binds URN_SPAWN; source selects uniformly from actual tag holders, positions the created entity at the broken block and calls addFreshEntity. Slime receives setSize(0,true). Configured check is not realized spawn probability.
mob_source.value: UrnBlock.spawnAfterBreak selects from #supplementaries:urn_spawn after a treasure-state check, nextFloat()<0.01, doTileDrops enabled and no tool enchantment in #minecraft:prevents_infested_spawns. Empty tag or failed entity creation yields no creature.

underground_surface_classification.basis: Uniform origin heights 16 through 96 above world bottom, followed by moonlight:below_heightmaps with MOTION_BLOCKING_NO_LEAVES and OCEAN_FLOOR_WG and below_sea_level true. Nine patch tries and six repetitions are attempts, not observed cache counts.

visual_discoverability.basis: Packaged feature and placement definitions; concealment and visibility distance are not measured.
visual_discoverability.source_form: Scattered treasure-state urns on supported air positions below terrain.

dispositions.rationale: A freestanding group of authored treasure vessels is one cache design. It is generated independently of a building or vegetation feature. Scattered positions and the number of successful urn placements are variants, not additional families.

families.rationale: All 22 configured variants feed one bridge selector and use the same bank-and-liquid-span placement and BridgeFeature. Material, length, intact/broken design and axis orientation vary within the river-crossing bridge family. The selector itself and three packaged templates outside its traced links are not additional families.

placement_eligibility.banks: Endpoint centers are length + 1 blocks apart. Both must canOcclude and have WORLD_SURFACE height <= sea level. At each endpoint, count the center plus contiguous qualifying lateral cells on each side, stopping that side at its first failure or width/2. Each endpoint count must reach numSolidBlocksNeeded.
placement_eligibility.sampling_plane: Sea level minus one. The generator subsequently anchors the template at sea level.
placement_eligibility.scope: These are the custom terrain checks. Biome filtering, selector variants and rarity modifiers remain separate packaged constraints; no world observation is inferred.
placement_eligibility.search: For each lateral offset from width/2 + widthOffset + 1 (inclusive) to 16 - width/2 - widthOffset (exclusive), try longitudinal offsets 0 through 15. Integer division is used. Swap X/Z roles for non-Z-axis variants. Return only the first valid candidate, or an empty stream.
placement_eligibility.source: BridgePlacement.getPositions in the captured generator manifest.
placement_eligibility.span: Every cell from lateral -width/2 through width/2 and longitudinal minWaterZ through maxWaterZ (inclusive) must satisfy BlockState.liquid at sea level minus one. The predicate does not specifically test water.
placement_eligibility.surface_classification: Surface liquid-crossing placement intent, supported by the bank heightmap and sea-level checks. This is not proof of player visibility or observed generation frequency.

generation.processing_stage: StructureTemplate.placeInWorld runs before the custom processor list is applied in order.
generation.rotation: isZAxis=false uses COUNTERCLOCKWISE_90; true retains default rotation.
generation.scope: Captured generation control flow, not observed placement success, discovery frequency or final support geometry. Full processor effects and placement eligibility still require reconciliation.
generation.selection: Randomly choose from remaining inline placed features; return on first successful place result, otherwise remove that candidate and continue until exhausted.
generation.success_limit: AbstractTemplateFeature discards the placeInWorld boolean. BridgeFeature returns true for a non-null loaded template; this does not prove all blocks were placed.

support_geometry.behavior: Replace the marker with the first supplied block state, then descend at fixed X/Z through air or liquid while Y > 0, using the second supplied state. Stop at Y <= 0 or a block that is neither air nor liquid.
support_geometry.limit: The descent uses literal Y=0, not the dimension minimum build height. setBlock return values are discarded; this is source-derived placement intent, not an observed completed pillar.
support_geometry.source: DynamicLegProcessor calls ITemplateFeatureProcessor.generatePillarDown for template support markers.
support_geometry.vertical_size: Template Y sizes describe the bridge body only. Supports may extend below that envelope; total occupied height depends on terrain and placement success.

generation.vertical_anchor: WorldGenLevel.getSeaLevel() replaces the incoming origin Y before template placement.

initialization.entrypoint: The NeoForge constructor calls the common init method. Common init scans the mod module package with YungAutoRegister.scanPackageForAnnotations, then calls Services.MODULES.loadModules().
initialization.neoforge_module_loader: The packaged NeoForgeModulesLoader delegates directly to IModulesLoader.loadModules. That default method contains only return, so this module-loader implementation performs no configuration registration.
initialization.scope: Verified direct entrypoint and module-loader implementation. Service selection and annotation-driven registration remain separate from this finding. This does not establish absence of all configuration, data-driven or external generation controls.

yungsbridges:bridges.mechanism: NeoForge add_features biome modifier to placed bridge_list, then configured multiple_attempt_single_random with inline placed bridge variants.
yungsbridges:bridges.relationship: One bridge family with 22 configured variants and 11 linked templates. Material, damage, length and rotation remain variants. Required effective attributes and provider coverage remain open.

template_content.scope: All fourteen packaged templates have empty entities and block_entities. Eleven are referenced by the verified bridge selector. biome_constraints.scope: Existing merged packaged tag resolution against registered biomes. Overlap with captured live dimension possible-biome lists is not proof of successful generation or observed removal. Optional absent members are not silently promoted to active biomes.

desert_generator_templates.anchor: ChillzoneDesertFeature and DesertGiantTorchFeature pass the ground anchor above(); DesertSmallRuinsFeature passes the ground anchor itself.
desert_generator_templates.centering: The helper subtracts half the template X/Z dimensions using integer division, leaves Y unchanged, and calls StructureTemplate.placeInWorld with default StructurePlaceSettings.
desert_generator_templates.scope: FeatureModule class/field AutoRegister annotations bind the yungsextras namespace and feature names to constructor-bound classes. Packaged configured type fields and captured template calls complete the three code-based links. Remaining terrain/content effects are still open; the JSON-explicit mapping remains separate.
desert_generator_templates.success_limit: The helper discards the placeInWorld boolean, then runs the processor list and returns the loaded template. Each of these classes returns whether the template is non-null. This is not proof that all template blocks were placed.
desert_generator_templates.template_call: Each class constructs its static ID with ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath and passes that ID to inherited createTemplateFromCenter.

desert_surface_generation.landing: All four descend through empty blocks while Y > 2. Each requires the landing block default state to match BlockTags.SAND and four selected positions at landing Y to satisfy BlockState.isSolid(). This is not a full-footprint ground check.
desert_surface_generation.placement: Chillzone, giant torch and obelisk center their template one block above landing. Small ruins center at landing Y. Obelisk reads the configured location; the other three fixed template links are recorded separately.
desert_surface_generation.processors: All four directly inherit AbstractNbtFeature and do not override useProcessors. The base initializes processors from useProcessors(), which returns a new empty ArrayList. These classes therefore add no custom post-placement processor through this path.
desert_surface_generation.scope: Source-derived terrain and placement rules only. Packaged chest and campfire contents remain recorded separately. This does not prove successful placement, full retained-stack content effects or observed visual discoverability.

desert_well_generation.brown_marker_rule: Choose cap nextInt(3)+2. In template filter order, select each brown stained glass marker with nextFloat()<0.1 until the cap; replace other markers with sand. If fewer than two were selected, convert previously unselected markers in order until two or until exhausted.
desert_well_generation.extra_loot_contents: One archaeology pool with one roll and diamond, emerald and gold_ingot item entries; no explicit weights or conditions. Packaged contents only, before external loot modification.
desert_well_generation.loot_assignment: placeSusSand requests SUSPICIOUS_SAND with update flag 3, discards the setBlock result, and assigns the loot table with position.asLong() as seed only if a BRUSHABLE_BLOCK entity is present.
desert_well_generation.processor_binding: DesertWellFeature.useProcessors selects only FeatureProcessorModule.DESERT_WELL_PROCESSOR. The module constructs DesertWellProcessor; its register helper returns the same instance. AbstractNbtFeature runs it after template placement.
desert_well_generation.scope: Source-supported placement and loot creation rules, not observed successful placements or reward counts. The shared template helper does not propagate placeInWorld failure. Family grouping and effective retained-stack loot modifications remain unresolved.
desert_well_generation.template_anchor: Pass the configured location to createTemplateFromCenter at landing position six blocks down. The unrotated template envelope is centered in X/Z by the inherited helper.
desert_well_generation.terrain: Descend through empty blocks while Y > 7. Require the landing block default state in BlockTags.SAND. At each depth 1 through 7 below the landing position, reject an empty block at the center or any of the four diagonal corners at the configured radius. These are non-empty checks, not full-volume solid-ground checks.
desert_well_generation.yellow_marker_rule: Choose independent budget nextInt(3)+2. In template filter order, select each yellow stained glass marker with nextFloat()<0.4 while budget remains, decrementing on selection; replace others with sand. There is no minimum-fill second pass.
